# Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 85m (version 10 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30) →
    # budget 100m; 240m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge
    # fail-fast fits inside the leg.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window; a wedged run is cancelled and re-dispatched
          # once (with the same distinct inputs → same distinct title).
          # Budget 110m = child worst-case 85m (#351: version 10 +
          # build-android 45 + submit-android 30; the #947 listing
          # deploy rides the submit-android job's slack) + 25m margin.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (all/none)' \
            --budget-seconds 6600 \
            -f android_content=all -f android_track=beta -f ios_content=none \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

    name: 'Leg: CLI + macOS desktop'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 325m (version 10 + build-macos 150×2 — the

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'cli'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=cli) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-macos.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Children derive version themselves (latest tag + 1 at their own
          # dispatch moment) — a tag pinned here would race auto_release and
          # could attach assets to a tag pointing at a different commit.
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-macos (create_release=true)") so a
          # concurrent human dispatch is never adopted; a wedged self-hosted
          # run is cancelled and re-dispatched once. Budget 340m = child
          # worst-case 325m (#351: version 10 + build-macos 150 ×2 arches
          # serialized on the one self-hosted runner + release-macos 15)
          # + 15m margin.
          rc=0

            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-macos (create_release=true)' \
            --budget-seconds 20400 \
            -f create_release=true \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

  website:
    name: 'Leg: Website'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 60m (pages build 45 + deploy 15) → budget
    # 75m; 180m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge fail-fast fits
    # (the old 45m leg made the self-heal dead code: 40m budget + 10m
    # appear window never completed inside it).
    timeout-minutes: 180
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'website')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Dispatch pages.yml and watch

blocks.text:
# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic."
  }

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWOR…

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets

      contents: read
      actions: write

        run: |

          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is

          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.

blocks.text:
name: Build macOS Release (Fa)

# Issue #343: the daily-publish CLI leg and a human can dispatch this
# workflow in the same window; the run-name embeds the input so the
# watcher's displayTitle match (the only distinguisher in the run-list
# API) never adopts someone else's run.
run-name: "build-macos (create_release=${{ inputs.create_release }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.0.2) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      create_release:
        description: 'Create GitHub Release'
        required: false
        default: 'true'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'true'
          - 'false'

# Release builds are never preempted (issue #194 pt 5, same principle as
# ci.yml: main/tag/release runs must not be cancelled mid-flight).
concurrency:
  group: Build macOS Release (Fa)-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

# SEC-08 (#796): minimal default — release-attaching jobs grant
# contents: write in their own job-level blocks.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWOR…

The version job at line ~67-115 uses fetch-depth: 0 under timeout-minutes: 10. Ticket fix options: blobless clone (`filter: blob:none`), raise ceiling to 20, audit siblings. Let me check build-macos.yml's Derive version too and grep all workflows for fetch-depth: 0 with tight timeouts. Also check for workflow-shape tests (bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py pattern).

#

  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m

  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351) + 20m margin — a healthy slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \

            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \

            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.

{
  "key": "gh-1477",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "[BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)",
    "description": "## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic."
  }

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi
          VERSION_CLEAN="${TAG#v}"
          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  build-android:
    name: Build Android AAB
    needs: version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Ceiling for the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351): gradle AAB
    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2
        with:
          channel: 'stable'
          cache: true

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # .env is gitignored but declared as a Flutter asset (flutter_dotenv);
      # newer flutter validates assets at build time, so the placeholder must
      # exist BEFORE flutter pub get (issue #368: aot_android_asset_bundle
      # died on "No file or variants found for asset: .env"). Content mirrors
      # the ci.yml/build-macos.yml incantation — bare `touch` is not enough
      # on ubuntu/flutter 3.47.4.
      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed
      # google-services.json is a placeholder (the google-services Gradle
      # plugin hard-fails without the file); overwrite it from the secret
      # when available.
      - name: Write google-services.json (Android)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json
            echo "google-services.json written (package: $(python3 -c "import json;print(json.load(open('flutter_app/android/app/google-services.json'))['client'][0]['client_info']['android_client_info']['package_name'])"))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON_BASE64 not set — building with the committed placeholder google-services.json"
          fi

      - name: Validate Android secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWOR…

# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.

# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on
# main (a manual dispatch, or the sibling daily leg's child in a
# single-leg run): a cross-run cancellation vector. Every dispatch is now
# independent; the #177 supersede-cancellation is intentionally traded
# away. The daily play/testflight legs dispatch this workflow CONCURRENTLY
# by design (#359 — decoupled from each other): their runs tell apart by
# the run-name correlation (#343), not by serialization, and the single
# self-hosted macOS runner serializes the iOS builds physically.
concurrency:
  group: Build Mobile Apps-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  version:
    name: Derive version
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Explicit ceiling so the daily watchers' budget arithmetic (#351) has
    # a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default.
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Derive build version
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          INPUT="${{ inputs.version }}"
          if [ -z "$INPUT" ] || [ "$INPUT" = "auto" ]; then
            LATEST=$(git tag --sort=-v:refname | grep -E '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$' | head -1 || echo "")
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.1.0"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi
          else
            TAG="$INPUT"
            [[ "$TAG" != v* ]] && TAG="v$TAG"
            echo "Using manual version: $TAG"
          fi

          echo "version=$VERSION_CLEAN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=$TAG" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # + bundletool validate historically ~20m, 45m is the slow-day bound.
    timeout-minutes: 45
    if: |
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'none' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != '' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'metadata_only' &&
      github.event.inputs.android_content != 'screenshots_only'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Java
        uses: actions/setup-java@de7274f081f381c8f8158605e0321c36c376e2e6 # v6.0.1
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'
          cache: 'gradle'

      - name: Setup Flutter
        uses: subosito/flutter-action@1a449444c387b1966244ae4d4f8c696479add0b2 # v2

          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=

      - name: Install dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # Mirrors the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist step: the committed

#

  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (493 > 360)
  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351) + 20m margin — a healthy slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.

blocks.text:
name: Build Mobile Apps

# Issue #343: the daily-publish TestFlight and Play legs dispatch this
# workflow in the same minute with different content inputs; the run-name
# embeds those inputs so `gh run list` displayTitle (the ONLY distinguisher
# the list API offers) tells the legs apart — each watcher matches its own
# run instead of latching a sibling's or a stale same-shaped one.
run-name: "build-mobile (${{ inputs.android_content }}/${{ inputs.ios_content }})"

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version (e.g. v0.1.0) or "auto" to increment patch'
        required: false
        default: 'auto'
      android_content:
        description: 'Android: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip Android entirely
          - all              # build + upload + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no upload, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no upload, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + upload only (no metadata, no screenshots)
      # #346: the daily Play leg passes android_track=beta; the input was
      # consumed (PLAY_TRACK below) but never declared, so every dispatch
      # died in seconds with HTTP 422 "Unexpected inputs provided".
      android_track:
        description: 'Android: Play upload track when android_content includes an upload (fastlane supply track)'
        required: false
        default: 'internal'
        type: choice
        options:
          - internal # owner/closed testing — manual dispatch default (issue #289 track policy)
          - beta     # external/open testing — the daily Play leg
          - production
      ios_content:
        description: 'iOS: what to deploy'
        required: false
        default: 'none'
        type: choice
        options:
          - none             # skip iOS entirely
          - all              # build + TestFlight + metadata + screenshots
          - metadata_only    # texts/descriptions only (no build, no TestFlight, no screenshots)
          - screenshots_only # screenshots only (no build, no TestFlight, no texts)
          - app_only         # build + TestFlight only (no metadata, no screenshots)

permissions:
  contents: write
  actions: write
  id-token: write

# Per-dispatch group (#351): the group is scoped by run_id so NO run can
# cancel another. The old ref-scoped group with cancel-in-progress made
# every fresh dispatch — including the daily watcher's wedge self-heal
# RE-DISPATCH (#344) — cancel whatever build-mobile run was in flight on

      - name: Setup Java

Rule I'll implement: for each fetch-depth: 0 job, add `filter: blob:none` unless it needs blobs (checkout for building/testing needs blobs!). Wait — ci.yml jobs that check out full history and then BUILD/TEST absolutely need blobs. filter: blob:none would lazy-fetch blobs on demand, which is fine functionally (git fetches missing blobs on demand) but might be slow for a full build checkout — actually no, for a working-tree checkout, checkout needs ALL blobs of the HEAD tree, so blobless clone would fetch them all anyway at checkout time = same cost. Blobless only helps when you don't materialize a full worktree. But actions/checkout always materializes a worktree. So filter: blob:none helps ONLY when the job never checks out files — but checkout action checks out files...

Hmm, actually for the version job: actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0 fetches all history AND all blobs of all revisions? No — git fetch of full history includes all blobs reachable from all commits/tags (full clone). With filter: blob:none, the initial fetch transfers only commits+trees, and then... does actions/checkout materialize the working tree? #

  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m

  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:

    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is

          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90

          rc=0

            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

# gh-1477: [BUG] build-mobile Derive version: fetch-depth:0 checkout outgrew its own 10-min timeout — daily leg cancelled mid-fetch (time bomb, grows with every tag)

## Description

## Problem

The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` (`:74`) runs `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full history + every tag) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. On 2026-10-10 the fetch outgrew the ceiling: job started 05:29:56.8Z, killed at 05:39:56.7Z (exactly 600s) mid-`git fetch` with `##[error]The operation was canceled.` — the whole TestFlight leg of the daily train collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551, issue #1472).

This is a **time bomb, not a flake**: the repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the full fetch only gets slower. The job needs the tag list and nothing else.

## Fix (pick, or combine)

1. **Blobless clone** — `fetch-depth: 0` + `filter: blob:none` (checkout v7 supports `filter`): full tag/commit metadata, no file blobs. Derive version reads only `git tag` — blobs are waste.
2. **Or skip checkout for the version math** — `git ls-remote --tags origin` / API call, no clone at all (checkout only if later steps in the job need files — they don't today).
3. **Raise the ceiling** as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2.

Also audit siblings: any other job doing `fetch-depth: 0` under a tight `timeout-minutes` has the same bomb (grep the workflows).

## Never-again

- Workflow-shape test (the `bench/terminal_bench/test_bench_workflow.py` pattern / existing workflow linters): a job whose steps only need tags must not pair `fetch-depth: 0` without `filter: blob:none` with `timeout-minutes < 20`.
- The daily watcher may treat a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class).

## Evidence

- Cancelled run: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/38027695551 (job `Derive version` log: start 05:29:56.8Z → `The operation was canceled.` 05:39:56.7Z)
- RCA comment: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/issues/1472#issuecomment-6095262371
- Twin Play leg (same sha, same minute) succeeded — the window is marginal, not deterministic.
