The plan job in daily-publish runs scripts/daily_plan.sh — needs main movement detection (commits) and tags. Blobless works (commits + tags kept, no blobs).

flake-watch: "quarantine PR branches from origin/main" — probably needs file content? Quarantine might create branches... Let me be careful. The minimum targeted fix per instructions: fix the root cause for the ticket job, and the ticket says "audit siblings: any other job doing fetch-depth: 0 under a tight timeout-minutes has the same bomb". So the audit is in scope.

Rule I'll implement: for each fetch-depth: 0 job, add `filter: blob:none` unless it needs blobs (checkout for building/testing needs blobs!). Wait — ci.yml jobs that check out full history and then BUILD/TEST absolutely need blobs. filter: blob:none would lazy-fetch blobs on demand, which is fine functionally (git fetches missing blobs on demand) but might be slow for a full build checkout — actually no, for a working-tree checkout, checkout needs ALL blobs of the HEAD tree, so blobless clone would fetch them all anyway at checkout time = same cost. Blobless only helps when you don't materialize a full worktree. But actions/checkout always materializes a worktree. So filter: blob:none helps ONLY when the job never checks out files — but checkout action checks out files...

Hmm, actually for the version job: actions/checkout with fetch-depth: 0 fetches all history AND all blobs of all revisions? No — git fetch of full history includes all blobs reachable from all commits/tags (full clone). With filter: blob:none, the initial fetch transfers only commits+trees, and then... does actions/checkout materialize the working tree? Yes it runs `git checkout`, which needs blobs for HEAD only, so it lazily fetches just HEAD's blobs (much smaller than ALL history blobs). So blobless is a big win when repo accumulates history: full clone transfers every blob ever; blobless transfers only current-tree blobs.

Even better: the ticket's option 2 — the version step only needs `git tag`, so we could skip fetching blobs AND skip the worktree? actions/checkout always checks out files. But fetching only HEAD blobs is small. Fine — filter: blob:none + fetch-depth: 0 is the recommended fix.

Actually, could also use `filter: tree:0` (commit-only) — but then `git checkout` would need to fetch trees+blobs lazily; actions/checkout with filter tree:0 works but checkout step may be slower. blob:none is the safer choice and the ticket suggests it.

For the guard test lint rule: "a job whose steps only need tags must not pair fetch-depth: 0 without filter: blob:none with timeout-minutes < 20".

#

  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m

  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:

    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch

        run: |

          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the

          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is

          rc=0

            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

#

  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +

  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351) + 20m margin — a healthy slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as

    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    # child wc 85m (version 10 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30) →

    # fail-fast fits inside the leg.
    timeout-minutes: 240

      contents: read
      actions: write

      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')

      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)

        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)

          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"

            exit 0
          fi

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch

          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

#

  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m

  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90

          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \
            --out-run-id run_id.txt || rc=$?
          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

          fetch-depth: 0

              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else

              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

blocks.text:
Bombs (fetch-depth: 0 + tight timeout):
- build-mobile.yml version: 10m
- build-macos.yml version: 10m
- daily-publish.yml plan: 10m
- ci.yml changes (Classify changes): 5m — needs base...head diff (commits/trees, no blobs needed for diff? `git diff base...head` needs blobs! Actually diff needs blob contents to compute diffs. Blobless would lazily fetch blobs — those blobs are needed anyway. Hmm, but for a diff classifier, blobs are needed. filter: blob:none would fetch blobs on demand during git diff — total transfer similar. But full clone transfers blobs of ALL history, not just the diff range. So blobless still helps, and checkout materializes HEAD tree. Still fine.)
- ci.yml coverage-gate: 5m
- ci.yml app-crap-gate: 6m
- ci.yml release: 15m
- ci.yml release-tag: 10m
- flake-watch: 15m

Ticket scope: "Also audit siblings: any other job doing fetch-depth: 0 under a tight timeout-minutes has the same bomb (grep the workflows)." The minimum targeted fix should cover the version/derive jobs which only need tags. For CI classifier jobs, blobs may be genuinely needed, and their timeouts are separate concerns. 

Decision: Fix strategy = add `filter: blob:none` to all fetch-depth: 0 checkouts whose jobs don't need historical blobs beyond what's demanded, and raise timeouts where < 20? That's getting big. Let me be more surgical:

The ticket's core fix (option 1+3 combined): `filter: blob:none` + timeout 10→20 for the Derive version job. Audit siblings and apply the same to jobs with the same shape (need only tags/commit metadata, not files): 
- build-macos.yml version (identical twin) — definitely fix.
- daily-publish.yml plan — runs daily_plan.sh: needs tags + main movement (git rev-list / log). Blobless fine. Fix: filter + timeout → 20.
- ci.yml release-tag (tag on push, 10m): what does it do? Probably creates tag from version — needs tags only. Let me check.
- ci.yml release (15m): bumps version, pushes commit — needs worktree (files) but only HEAD blobs. Still, bump-push writes files. filter blob:none still works (HEAD blobs fetched on demand). But checkout materializes the full worktree anyway; the savings from blobless = not fetching historical blobs. Fine.
- flake-watch (15m): quarantine PRs — creates branches, runs scripts that probably need file contents.
- ci.yml changes/coverage-gate/app-crap-gate (5-6m): need file diffs.

Hmm. For the CI jobs that need blobs for diffing, filter: blob:none doesn't reduce total transfer much (the needed blobs get fetched on demand), but reduces clone fetch time only marginally. The real issue in the ticket is jobs that ONLY need tags fetching everything.

I think the right minimum fix:
1. build-mobile.yml + build-macos.yml version jobs: `filter: blob:none`, timeout 10→20. (The ticket job + identical twin.)
2. daily-publish.yml plan job: same (tag/change-detection only). Actually wait — does daily_plan.sh need file contents? "Detect main movement" — likely `git rev-parse`, `git log`, tags. Let me verify.
3. Guard test: new Dart test `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` enforcing: any checkout step with `fetch-depth: 0` must have `filter: blob:none`, and if job timeout < 20 then filter is REQUIRED... Actually the never-again rule: "a job whose steps only need tags must not pair fetch-depth: 0 without filter: blob:none with timeout-minutes < 20".

Simpler enforceable rule: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must also set `filter: blob:none` (blobless is strictly better for CI since checkout only materializes HEAD anyway — historical blobs are almost never needed in CI jobs; and when they are, git lazily fetches them). Is that true for all these jobs? For `git diff base...head`, blobs fetched on demand = same total. For checkout worktree, HEAD blobs fetched on demand. So blobless never changes correctness, only laziness. One caveat: filter with local git < 2.27? GitHub runners have modern git. actions/checkout v7 supports filter (ticket says so).

So the clean never-again lint: **every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout in .github/workflows must carry `filter: blob:none`**. Plus keep timeout seatbelts. Should I also raise timeouts? The ticket says "Raise the ceiling as a seatbelt (10 → 20m) regardless of 1/2". I'll raise the version/plan jobs' ceilings to 20.

But careful about #351 watcher budget arithmetic — raising version job timeout 10→20 increases the daily watch budget chain. Let me check if any test or script hard-codes "10" for the version job timeout. Let me search.

#

  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (493 > 360)
  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351) + 20m margin — a healthy slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \

            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \

            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

# Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 85m (version 10 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30) →
    # budget 100m; 240m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge
    # fail-fast fits inside the leg.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}

  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets

    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.

      contents: read

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

#

  # 240 ✓, website 163 ≤ 180 ✓, addin 133 ≤ 150 ✓. testflight (493 > 360)
  # and cli (693 > 360) CANNOT fit two full budgets under GitHub's 360m
  # job cap — their first wedge still self-heals (cancel at budget +
  # re-dispatch ≈ budget+13m), and a second wedge is bounded by the leg
  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'testflight'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344): correlates OUR run by the
          # child's run-name ("build-mobile (none/all)" — displayTitle is
          # the only distinguisher in the run-list API), newest match in a
          # tight window; a wedged run (self-hosted slot lost, #344) is
          # cancelled and re-dispatched once before failing.
          # Budget 240m = child worst-case 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90
          # + submit-ios 120, #351) + 20m margin — a healthy slow TestFlight
          # submit (Apple processing can legitimately take the full 90m
          # ASC wait + 15m verify) is never cancelled by the watcher.
          rc=0
          bash scripts/dispatch_and_watch.sh build-mobile.yml \
            --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" --ref main \
            --title 'build-mobile (none/all)' \
            --budget-seconds 14400 \
            -f android_content=none -f ios_content=all \

          if [ -s run_id.txt ]; then
            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          exit "$rc"

blocks.text:
# Independent of the testflight leg (#359). The #348 serialization was
    # a mitigation for the #343 sibling-dispatch race; #351 eliminated that
    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child
    # runs as "build-mobile (all/none)", the testflight leg's as
    # "(none/all)"), NEWEST match, a tight 30s window, and build-mobile's
    # per-run_id concurrency group (no dispatch can cancel another). With
    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).
    #
    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS
    #     runner (which already serializes physically with the cli leg's
    #     build-macos children — that pair has always been independent).
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic (unchanged by #359 — only the leg's START moved):
    # child wc 85m (version 10 + build-android 45 + submit-android 30) →
    # budget 100m; 240m leg ≥ 2×budget + 15m, so the second-wedge
    # fail-fast fits inside the leg.
    timeout-minutes: 240
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'play')
    outputs:
      run_url: ${{ steps.dispatch.outputs.run_url }}
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      # Secrets presence is checked in the first step — while the Play
      # upload keystore/service account are not configured, the leg green-
      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).
      PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON: ${{ secrets.PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Inject failure (test)
        if: inputs.inject_failure == 'play'
        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=play) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Skip without Play secrets (green-neutral)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          missing=""
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS"
          [ -z "${ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD:-}" ] && missing="$missing ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD"
          if [ -z "${PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON:-}" ]; then
            missing="$missing PLAY_STORE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON"
          fi
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::notice::Play secrets not configured (missing:${missing}) — the Android leg skips green-neutrally until the upload keystore + Play service account secrets exist (issue #289 owner checklist)."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "All Play secrets present — dispatching the Android build+upload."

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # all: build + Play upload + LISTING deploy (issue #947) — the
          # listing lane replaces the whole image set per locale + device
          # type and verifies it via edits.images.list, so the listing can
          # never trail the committed goldens by more than one train.
          # beta = the external/open testing track, mirroring the iOS leg's
          # external TestFlight group (#239 pattern).
          # Shared watcher (issues #343/#344). Since #359 the TestFlight
          # sibling leg fires CONCURRENTLY with this one (both needs: plan)
          # and dispatches the SAME workflow in the same minute —
          # correlation is by the child's run-name ("build-mobile
          # (all/none)" vs the sibling's "(none/all)", pinned by
          # test), never by "first run in the window", with newest-match +
          # the 30s window; a wedged run is cancelled and re-dispatched
          # once (with the same distinct inputs → same distinct title).
          # Budget 110m = child worst-case 85m (#351: version 10 +
          # build-android 45 + submit-android 30; the #947 listing
          # deploy rides the submit-android job's slack) + 25m margin.
          rc=0

  testflight:
    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets
    # (493m) exceed GitHub's 360m cap — a second wedge is bounded by this
    # leg timeout, not the watcher fail-fast.
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: write
    if: >-
      (needs.plan.outputs.changed == 'true' || inputs.force == true) &&
      (inputs.legs == '' || inputs.legs == 'all' || inputs.legs == 'testflight')
    outputs:

    env:

      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

        run: |
          echo "::error::injected failure (inject_failure=testflight) — exercising the self-filing issue path, nothing dispatched"
          exit 1

      - name: Dispatch build-mobile.yml and watch
        id: dispatch

    # race structurally — exact displayTitle correlation (this leg's child

    # the race gone the needs-edge only bought harm: a cancelled testflight
    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).

    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).

      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

#

  # timeout instead of the watcher's fail-fast; both children carry
  # per-job server-side timeouts (#344) so a wedged job self-fails even
  # without the watcher.

    name: 'Leg: TestFlight'
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # #351 arithmetic: child wc 220m (version 10 + build-ios 90 +
    # submit-ios 120) → budget 240m; 360m leg > budget. Two full budgets

      contents: read
      actions: write

            echo "run_url=https://github.com/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/actions/runs/$(cat run_id.txt)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in

    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

    # watcher skipped Play behind it and the edge added up to 360m of start
    # latency (one leg's external blocker stopped the train — run
    # 34827074052, BETA_REVIEW_CONTACT_EMAIL user-owned).

    # The two residual #346 concerns are handled structurally, not by
    # ordering:
    #   * same-tag convergence — both children independently derive
    #     latest-tag+1, so they can attach to ONE release concurrently;
    #     release_attach_or_create.sh is race-idempotent (a lost create
    #     uploads into the winner's release) with an ownership-scoped draft
    #     guard, and the asset sets never collide (AAB vs IPA).
    #   * runner contention — none: the Android chain is all GitHub-hosted
    #     runners; only build-ios touches the single self-hosted macOS

      # skips with a notice (existing neutral-skip leg semantics); it goes
      # live the moment the owner sets them (issue #289).

      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
      ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
      ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
      ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in

    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

# Explicit ceiling so the daily cli watcher's budget arithmetic (#351)
    # has a real per-job bound instead of GitHub's 360m default. gh-1477:
    # 10m was a time bomb — the full-history fetch outgrew its twin in
    # build-mobile (run 38027695551). 20m + the blobless filter below.
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      tag: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # gh-1477: this job reads ONLY `git tag` — a full clone transfers
          # every blob ever written and the repo grows daily, so the fetch
          # outgrew the old 10m ceiling (run 38027695551). Blobless keeps
          # full tag/commit metadata without the blobs.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
            if [ -z "$LATEST" ]; then
              TAG="v0.0.1"
              echo "No previous tag found — starting at $TAG"
            else
              MAJOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\1/')
              MINOR=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\2/')
              PATCH=$(echo "$LATEST" | sed 's/v\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)\.\([0-9]*\)/\3/')
              PATCH=$((PATCH + 1))
              TAG="v${MAJOR}.${MINOR}.${PATCH}"
              echo "Previous tag: $LATEST → auto-increment to $TAG"
            fi

        with:

      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

# jq selector: optional exact displayTitle match (#343).
title_select=""
if [ -n "$title" ]; then
  title_select=" | select(.displayTitle == \"${title}\")"
fi

dispatch() {
  gh workflow run "$workflow" --repo "$repo" --ref "$ref" ${inputs[@]+"${inputs[@]}"}
}

# The id of OUR run: workflow_dispatch runs created at/after the floor,
# matching --title when given, NEWEST of the matches (#343).
find_run_id() {
  local floor="$1"
  gh run list --repo "$repo" --workflow "$workflow" --event workflow_dispatch \
    --limit 20 --json databaseId,createdAt,displayTitle \
    --jq "[.[] | select((.createdAt | fromdateiso8601) >= $floor)${title_select}] | sort_by(.createdAt) | .[-1].databaseId // 0" \
    2>/dev/null || echo 0
}

wait_for_run() {
  local floor="$1" id=0 i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt "$appear_attempts" ]; do
    id=$(find_run_id "$floor")
    if [ "$id" -gt 0 ] 2>/dev/null; then echo "$id"; return 0; fi
    sleep "$appear_poll"
    i=$((i + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

content.thinking:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

messages.preview: The watcher change is a "may" in the ticket — I'll defer it and document why. Checking the full suite:

blocks.text:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):
1. `filter: blob:none` on every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout — full tag/commit metadata, no historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches. Defuses the growth (metadata grows ~KBs/day vs blobs MBs/day).
2. Seatbelt: the three metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) 10 → 20m.
3. `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together (worst-cases +10m; testflight budget 14400→15000s, cli 20400→21000s, play stays 6600s at its exact margin) in `daily-publish.yml` AND `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
4. Never-again workflow-shape lint: `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` (AC1: full-history checkouts must be blobless; AC2: metadata-only daily-train jobs carry ≥20m).

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (not returned).

while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1

blocks.text:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

{"content":"# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):
1. `filter: blob:none` on every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout — full tag/commit metadata, no historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches. Defuses the growth (metadata grows ~KBs/day vs blobs MBs/day).
2. Seatbelt: the three metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) 10 → 20m.
3. `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together (worst-cases +10m; testflight budget 14400→15000s, cli 20400→21000s, play stays 6600s at its exact margin) in `daily-publish.yml` AND `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
4. Never-again workflow-shape lint: `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` (AC1: full-history checkouts must be blobless; AC2: metadata-only daily-train jobs carry ≥20m).

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (not returned).

    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done
