while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

blocks.text:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

{"content":"# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):
1. `filter: blob:none` on every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout — full tag/commit metadata, no historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches. Defuses the growth (metadata grows ~KBs/day vs blobs MBs/day).
2. Seatbelt: the three metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) 10 → 20m.
3. `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together (worst-cases +10m; testflight budget 14400→15000s, cli 20400→21000s, play stays 6600s at its exact margin) in `daily-publish.yml` AND `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
4. Never-again workflow-shape lint: `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` (AC1: full-history checkouts must be blobless; AC2: metadata-only daily-train jobs carry ≥20m).

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (not returned).

while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

blocks.text:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

{"content":"# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):
1. `filter: blob:none` on every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout — full tag/commit metadata, no historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches. Defuses the growth (metadata grows ~KBs/day vs blobs MBs/day).
2. Seatbelt: the three metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) 10 → 20m.
3. `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together (worst-cases +10m; testflight budget 14400→15000s, cli 20400→21000s, play stays 6600s at its exact margin) in `daily-publish.yml` AND `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
4. Never-again workflow-shape lint: `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` (AC1: full-history checkouts must be blobless; AC2: metadata-only daily-train jobs carry ≥20m).

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (not returned).

while :; do
    status=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status,conclusion \
      --jq '.status + "/" + (.conclusion // "-")' 2>/dev/null || echo "error/-")
    if [ "${status%%/*}" = "completed" ]; then break; fi
    if [ $(( $(date +%s) - started )) -gt "$budget" ]; then
      if [ "$attempt" -ge 2 ]; then
        echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id still unfinished after ${budget}s on the SECOND attempt — runner pool suspect (issue #344); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      echo "::warning::$workflow run $run_id unfinished after ${budget}s — cancelling and re-dispatching once (issue #344 self-heal); https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id"
      gh run cancel "$run_id" --repo "$repo" \
        || echo "::warning::cancel of run $run_id failed (already gone?)"
      # Bounded wait for the cancel to land — a wedged worker may never
      # process it, so never block the re-dispatch on it.
      cancel_deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + cancel_wait ))
      while [ "$(date +%s)" -lt "$cancel_deadline" ]; do
        s=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$repo" --json status --jq '.status' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
        [ "$s" = "completed" ] && break
        sleep "$poll"
      done
      attempt=$((attempt + 1))
      continue 2
    fi
    sleep "$poll"
  done

  conclusion="${status#*/}"
  echo "$workflow run $run_id conclusion: $conclusion"
  if [ "$conclusion" = "success" ]; then exit 0; fi
  echo "::error::$workflow run $run_id concluded $conclusion — https://github.com/$repo/actions/runs/$run_id" >&2
  exit 1
done

blocks.text:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

{"content":"# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):
1. `filter: blob:none` on every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout — full tag/commit metadata, no historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches. Defuses the growth (metadata grows ~KBs/day vs blobs MBs/day).
2. Seatbelt: the three metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) 10 → 20m.
3. `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together (worst-cases +10m; testflight budget 14400→15000s, cli 20400→21000s, play stays 6600s at its exact margin) in `daily-publish.yml` AND `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
4. Never-again workflow-shape lint: `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` (AC1: full-history checkouts must be blobless; AC2: metadata-only daily-train jobs carry ≥20m).

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (not returned).

messages.preview: The watcher change is a "may" in the ticket — I'll defer it and document why. Checking the full suite:

blocks.text:
The ticket's second never-again: "The daily watcher may treat a leg-run cancelled by its own job-timeout as re-dispatchable once (it already re-dispatches wedged runs; a 0ms-jobs cancellation is the same infra class)."

Current behavior: a run concluded `cancelled` (by its own job timeout) → falls out of the poll loop with conclusion != success → error exit, no re-dispatch. The ticket says "may" — optional. Implementing it would change watcher behavior for ALL cancellations, including cancellations caused by... hmm, when would a run be legitimately cancelled? By the watcher's own wedge self-heal (attempt 1 cancels — but that's the run being watched, and after cancel it re-dispatches; the cancelled original isn't re-evaluated since we `continue 2`). Other sources: manual cancel, concurrency (build-mobile has cancel-in-progress: false), github outage. Treating `cancelled` as infra-class and re-dispatching once mirrors the wedge heal.

This is a behavior change with risk: a human cancelling a run would trigger a re-dispatch. The ticket hedges with "may". TDD rule: minimum targeted fix for the root cause only. The root cause (fetch outgrew timeout) is fixed by blobless+20m+lint. I'll note the watcher item as a deliberately deferred option in the PR notes rather than implement it — it's flagged "may", carries its own risks (re-dispatching human-cancelled runs), and deserves its own ticket. Hmm — but "Never-again" sections in these tickets are usually expected ACs. The first never-again (workflow-shape test) I've implemented. The second is phrased "may treat ... as re-dispatchable once" — permissive, not mandatory. I'll state in Notes why it's deferred.

Actually, let me reconsider: implement it? The re-dispatch of a cancelled run: after `conclusion="${status#*/}"`, if conclusion == "cancelled" and attempt == 1, warn + attempt=2 + continue 2 (re-dispatch). But careful: the watcher's OWN cancel in the wedge heal sets the watched run to cancelled... no — after the wedge-heal cancel, it does `continue 2` which re-dispatches and watches the NEW run; the old run's conclusion is never checked. But there's a subtle case: if the run completes between budget expiry and cancel (lands as cancelled by our own cancel) — we don't check its conclusion; we just re-dispatch. Fine.

Risk: human cancels a daily child run → watcher re-dispatches it once. That's arguably the desired infra-class behavior per the ticket. But it also re-dispatches a run cancelled by GitHub for policy reasons (rare). Implementation is small. However — changing watcher behavior requires updating dispatch_watch_test.dart behavioral tests (they stub gh and assert on cancel/re-dispatch flows). That's a meaningful chunk of work and the test file pins "cancelled and re-dispatched once" for the wedge case.

Given the guidance "minimum targeted fix for the root cause ONLY" and the ticket's own "may", I'll defer it and document. The core AC (workflow-shape test + fix) is done.

{"content":"# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):
1. `filter: blob:none` on every `fetch-depth: 0` checkout — full tag/commit metadata, no historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff actually touches. Defuses the growth (metadata grows ~KBs/day vs blobs MBs/day).
2. Seatbelt: the three metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) 10 → 20m.
3. `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together (worst-cases +10m; testflight budget 14400→15000s, cli 20400→21000s, play stays 6600s at its exact margin) in `daily-publish.yml` AND `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
4. Never-again workflow-shape lint: `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` (AC1: full-history checkouts must be blobless; AC2: metadata-only daily-train jobs carry ≥20m).

**Previous attempt**: none — fresh bug (not returned).

{"content":"# gh-1477 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `Derive version` job in `build-mobile.yml` was cancelled exactly 600s in (mid-`git fetch`), collapsing the whole daily TestFlight leg to `cancelled` (run 38027695551).

**Root cause**: `.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml`, job `version` (line 74): `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` performs a FULL clone — every commit, tag, **and every blob ever written** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a release tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the fixed ceiling. The job's only use of the checkout is `git tag --sort=-v:refname` — tag metadata. Blobs were pure waste.

**Impact**: Daily release train leg collapses to `cancelled`; deterministic time bomb that re-fires with every new tag. Twin bombs found by the audit: `build-macos.yml` job `version` (identical shape), `daily-publish.yml` job `plan` (10m ceiling, full clone, reads tags/commit metadata only), and 9 more `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across `ci.yml` (5), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml`.

**Fix approach** (ticket options 1 + 3 combined, applied repo-wide per the ticket's sibling audit):

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- The pre-existing `test/cli/` VM crash blocks a single-shot full-suite green in this environment (it dies before `test/cube`, `test/mcp`, `test/providers`, `test/session`, `test/wire`, … run); those were verified via the separate remainder run above. Worth its own infrastructure issue.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- The pre-existing `test/cli/` VM crash blocks a single-shot full-suite green in this environment (it dies before `test/cube`, `test/mcp`, `test/providers`, `test/session`, `test/wire`, … run); those were verified via the separate remainder run above. Worth its own infrastructure issue.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.

Done. gh-1477 is fixed with all outputs written and everything committed.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `build-mobile.yml` `Derive version` ran `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone — every blob ever written) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

**Fix (ticket options 1+3, repo-wide per the sibling audit)**:
- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `build-mobile.yml` `Derive version` ran `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone — every blob ever written) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

**Fix (ticket options 1+3, repo-wide per the sibling audit)**:
- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- The pre-existing `test/cli/` VM crash blocks a single-shot full-suite green in this environment (it dies before `test/cube`, `test/mcp`, `test/providers`, `test/session`, `test/wire`, … run); those were verified via the separate remainder run above. Worth its own infrastructure issue.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `build-mobile.yml` `Derive version` ran `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone — every blob ever written) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

**Fix (ticket options 1+3, repo-wide per the sibling audit)**:
- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.

Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `build-mobile.yml` `Derive version` ran `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone — every blob ever written) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

**Fix (ticket options 1+3, repo-wide per the sibling audit)**:
- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- The pre-existing `test/cli/` VM crash blocks a single-shot full-suite green in this environment (it dies before `test/cube`, `test/mcp`, `test/providers`, `test/session`, `test/wire`, … run); those were verified via the separate remainder run above. Worth its own infrastructure issue.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `build-mobile.yml` `Derive version` ran `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone — every blob ever written) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

**Fix (ticket options 1+3, repo-wide per the sibling audit)**:
- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).

{"content":"### Root Cause

- `build-mobile.yml` job `Derive version` checked out with `fetch-depth: 0` — a **full clone (every blob ever written)** — under `timeout-minutes: 10`. The repo gains a tag + commits daily, so the transfer grew monotonically until it outgrew the ceiling: the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-`git fetch` and the daily TestFlight leg collapsed to `cancelled` (run 38027695551). The job only reads `git tag` — blobs were pure waste.

### Fix

- `build-mobile.yml` / `build-macos.yml` (`Derive version`) + `daily-publish.yml` (`plan`): `filter: blob:none` on the full-history checkout (tag/commit metadata, no blobs) and ceiling 10 → 20m as the seatbelt.
- Sibling audit (ticket ask): `filter: blob:none` added to **every** `fetch-depth: 0` checkout repo-wide — `ci.yml` (5 jobs), `flake-watch.yml`, `shard-rebalance.yml`, and the two release-notes jobs in `build-mobile.yml`/`build-macos.yml` (they read commit messages, never historical blobs; git lazy-fetches the rare blob a diff touches).
- `#351` watch-budget arithmetic recomputed together: worst-cases +10m (testflight 220→230, play 85→95, cli 325→335); budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s` (play stays `6600s` at its exact ≥15m margin); mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- Never-again lint: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — AC1: any `fetch-depth: 0` checkout must carry `filter: blob:none`; AC2: the metadata-only daily-train jobs (derive version ×2, daily plan) must keep `timeout-minutes ≥ 20`.

### Test Coverage

- `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — 19 tests; **RED before the fix** (9 failures: 6 workflows missing the filter + 3 jobs under the 20m seatbelt), **GREEN after**.
- `test/dispatch_watch_test.dart` — 28 tests pass (updated arithmetic table).
- Related suites (`release_flow_race`, `release_hygiene`, `nightly_desktop_leg_guard`, `store_automation_guard`) — 149 tests pass.
- Full suite: two full runs — everything up to `test/cli/` passed with zero failures; the run then hits a **deterministic pre-existing Dart VM native crash** (`malloc_consolidate(): unaligned chunk … Aborted`) in the `test/cli/` PTY suite — reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613` (verified in a clean worktree) and is unrelated to this diff. The remainder (lexically after `test/cli/`) was run separately: **6191 passed, 53 skipped, 13 failed — the same 13 fail identically on the base commit** (`test/integration/` headless/yolo/tools/backend e2e, environment-dependent). No regressions attributable to this change.

### Notes

- `blobless + fetch-depth: 0` keeps full tag/commit metadata; `git checkout` materializes the HEAD tree by lazy-fetching only those blobs, so no job's behavior changes — only the transfer shrinks.
- The ticket's second never-again (watcher re-dispatching a leg-run `cancelled` by its own job timeout) was deliberately **not** implemented: it is phrased as "may", changes watcher semantics for human-cancelled runs too, and deserves its own ticket + behavioral tests in `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- The pre-existing `test/cli/` VM crash blocks a single-shot full-suite green in this environment (it dies before `test/cube`, `test/mcp`, `test/providers`, `test/session`, `test/wire`, … run); those were verified via the separate remainder run above. Worth its own infrastructure issue.

Done. gh-1477 is fixed with all outputs written and everything committed.

## Summary

**Root cause**: `build-mobile.yml` `Derive version` ran `actions/checkout` with `fetch-depth: 0` (full clone — every blob ever written) under `timeout-minutes: 10`. Daily repo growth made the fetch outgrow the ceiling; the job was killed at exactly 600s mid-fetch, collapsing the TestFlight leg (run 38027695551).

**Fix (ticket options 1+3, repo-wide per the sibling audit)**:
- **`filter: blob:none`** on all 12 `fetch-depth: 0` checkouts across 6 workflows (derive-version ×2, daily plan, ci.yml ×5, flake-watch, shard-rebalance, release-notes ×2) — blobs were never read; git lazy-fetches on the rare touch.
- **Ceiling 10 → 20m** on the three metadata-only daily-train jobs.
- **#351 arithmetic recomputed together**: worst-cases +10m; budgets testflight `14400→15000s`, cli `20400→21000s`; mirrored in `daily-publish.yml` comments and `dispatch_watch_test.dart`.
- **Never-again lint**: new `test/workflow_fetch_shape_guard_test.dart` — was RED (9 failures) before the fix, GREEN after (19 tests).

**Verification**: guard test + dispatch_watch (47) and the four related workflow/hygiene suites (149) pass. The full suite was run twice: everything before `test/cli/` passed with zero failures, then the Dart VM deterministically core-dumps in the PTY suite — **reproduces identically on base commit `2dfc613`**, so pre-existing. The remainder ran separately: 6191 passed / 13 failed / 53 skipped, and those same 13 `test/integration/` e2e failures reproduce identically on base — no regressions from this change.

**Deliberately deferred** (documented in the PR notes): the "watcher re-dispatches job-timeout-cancelled runs" idea is phrased "may" in the ticket and changes watcher semantics — deserves its own ticket.
